title: Schematic neighborhoods at points of local dimension at most one
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] whose diagonal $X\to X\times_SX$ is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume that $X$ is locally Noetherian, meaning that every etale scheme chart is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $a:V\to X$ be an etale morphism from a scheme, and $v\in V$, such that $\dim\mathcal O_{V,v}\leq1$, with ring dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then there is an open subspace $U\subseteq X$ containing $a(v)$ which is represented by an $S$-scheme. An open subspace means a subfunctor whose pullback along every map from a scheme is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. No bound on the global dimension of $X$ or on the dimension of $S$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0ADD, lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus. Codimension is the local-ring dimension, equivalently computed on any etale scheme chart, as in spaces-properties.tex, definition-dimension-local-ring.

proof.text: Put $x=a(v)$. By [lem-sfb-space-local-dimension-chart-invariance], the chart hypothesis gives $\delta_X(x)\leq1$. Choose an open neighbourhood $Z$ of $x$ admitting a surjective etale map $T\to Z$ with $T$ affine and with $Z\to S$ factoring through an affine open $S_0\subseteq S$, by [lem-a1-space-affine-atlas-open-cover]. The open $Z$ is quasi-compact by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] and locally Noetherian: any etale scheme chart of $Z$ is also an etale chart of $X$. Its diagonal over $S_0$ is the restriction of that of $X/S$ and is closed on scheme tests: pullbacks of closed immersions are closed immersions [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. For affine etale charts $A,B\to Z$, $A\times_ZB$ is therefore a closed subscheme of the affine scheme $A\times_{S_0}B$; it is affine and quasi-compact [def-weil-closed-immersion, lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Viewing $Z$ as an absolute algebraic space by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers], the affine-pair criterion [lem-sfb-etale-affine-pairs-test-quasiseparated] makes it absolutely quasi-separated. Thus $Z$ is Noetherian. Restricting the given pointed chart to $Z$ leaves its stalk at $v$ unchanged, so $\delta_Z(x)\leq1$.

source.place: Tag 0ADD, lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus, first paragraph, reduction to a quasi-compact separated Noetherian neighbourhood; affine-base refinement uses Properties of Spaces 03FY

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-finite-scheme-cover] over $S_0$ to obtain a scheme $Y$ and a finite surjective $f:Y\to Z$. Put $P=Y\times_ZT$. This is a scheme finite over $T$, while $P\to Y$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The affine scheme $T$ is locally Noetherian by the hypothesis on $X$. A finite morphism is locally of finite type: on affines finite module generators are also algebra generators [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Hence [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] gives that $P$ is locally Noetherian. Etale-local descent [lem-trf-etale-local-noetherian-descent] applied to $P\to Y$ proves that $Y$ is locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0ADD, lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus, first paragraph, finite scheme cover (Limits of Spaces 09YC); source Noetherianity checked by Morphisms 01T6 and Descent 034C

proof.text: The finite morphism $f$ is integral on every scheme test by [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft]. Thus [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence] makes $f$ separated. Composing with the separated map $Z\to S_0$ gives a separated scheme morphism $Y\to S_0$ by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Since $S_0$ is affine, [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated] proves absolute separatedness of $Y$. This is the separatedness required for the absolute groupoid lemma below; no separatedness of the original base $S$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 0ADD, lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus, first paragraph, separatedness of the scheme covering the affine-base neighbourhood

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology], $f$ is locally quasi-finite. Applying [lem-sfb-space-local-ring-dimension-quasifinite] at each $y\in f^{-1}(x)$ gives $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}\leq\delta_Z(x)\leq1$. Only the local dimensions at points of this fibre are bounded; no dimension bound for all of $Y$ or $Z$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0ADD, lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus, first paragraph, dimension bound from Decent Spaces 0ABW

proof.text: Form the scheme $R=Y\times_ZY$ using diagonal representability [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The projections $s,t$ are finite by [lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology]. This is an absolute groupoid [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]: on test schemes its arrows are pairs $(b,c)$ with $f(b)=f(c)$, with identity $(b,b)$, inverse $(c,b)$, and composition $((b,c),(c,d))\mapsto(b,d)$. These formulas verify the groupoid laws. Choose $y\in f^{-1}(x)$ by surjectivity. Its orbit equals $f^{-1}(x)$: every arrow has equal image under $f$, and conversely any two points over $x$ lift to a point of $Y\times_ZY$ by [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point]. Steps 2--4 supply local Noetherianity, absolute separatedness and the local dimension bounds on this orbit. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-groupoid-height-one-affine-open] to get an affine open $W\subseteq Y$ containing the orbit and satisfying $s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$.

source.place: Tag 0ADD, lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus, first paragraph and second paragraph, applying More on Groupoids 0ABI to the finite equivalence relation

proof.text: For $w\in W$ and $y\in Y$ with $f(y)=f(w)$, [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] supplies an arrow between them. Invariance of $W$ forces $y\in W$. Thus $f^{-1}(f(W))=W$. Since $f$ is closed and surjective [lem-sfb-finite-space-morphism-topology], $|Z|\setminus f(W)=f(|Y|\setminus W)$ is closed. The open-subspace correspondence [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] gives an open subspace $Z^{\prime}\subseteq Z$ with point set $f(W)$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], the pullback $Y\times_ZZ^{\prime}$ is the open subscheme with point set $W$, hence equals $W$. Therefore $W\to Z^{\prime}$ is a base change of $f$, finite and surjective, and $x\in|Z^{\prime}|$.

source.place: Tag 0ADD, lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus, second paragraph, descending the invariant open via closed surjectivity

proof.text: The continuous surjection $W\to Z^{\prime}$ has quasi-compact source because $W$ is affine [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; pull back any open cover and take a finite subcover. Hence $Z^{\prime}$ is quasi-compact. It is locally Noetherian by restriction, and is quasi-separated since it is a quasi-compact open subspace of the quasi-separated space $Z$ [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence]. Thus it is Noetherian. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-finite-affine-descent] to the finite surjection $W\to Z^{\prime}$ to obtain an affine scheme representing $Z^{\prime}$. The composite open subspace $Z^{\prime}\subseteq Z\subseteq X$ contains $x$. Its representing scheme has the induced map to $S_0\subseteq S$, so it is the required $S$-scheme neighbourhood.

source.place: Tag 0ADD, lemma-codim-1-point-in-schematic-locus, second paragraph, finite affine descent (Cohomology of Spaces 07VP) and conclusion

lean.statement: theorem exists_scheme_open_of_stalk_dimension_le_one {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hsep : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 X.obj.obj) (𝟙 X.obj.obj))) (hnoeth : ∀ (T : Over S) (t : yoneda.obj T ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsEtale t → IsLocallyNoetherian T.left) (V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.obj.obj) (ha : IsEtale a) (v : V.left) (hdim : ringKrullDim (V.left.presheaf.stalk v) ≤ (1 : WithBot ℕ∞)) : ∃ (U : Over S) (j : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) j ∧ schemePointMap a v ∈ Set.range (schemePointMap j)
